title: The voice of Yaakov: how the heart unites with thought and speech, Leah and Rachel
overview:
Chapter 37 begins the unions of Yisroel and Yaakov, the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*, with Leah and Rachel, thought and speech. First it explains the voice. The breath of the heart is made of spiritual fire, water and wind, *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, and you can hear them: a hoarse voice, a clear one, and the blend of joy and sadness of a great singer, who sings with feeling more than technique. All life beats in and out: the heart, the breath, the brain, music. The lungs push a wind through the reed of the larynx, and the emotions move the bellows, so the voice that is heard carries the feeling.

What stays in the heart is not yet the king's word; so whether a man will be righteous or wicked is thought before his birth, never said. The inner voice, the reason behind the feeling, cannot be heard in the voice, only in the letters of thought, and thought keeps a feeling alive: that is why counting to ten works. The chapter ends with four unions, the order of the flow, and a class like this one: holiness coming into speech, like *Shabbos*.

terms.gloss: the inner voice, not heard in the voice: the reason behind the emotion, from the mochin
fire, water and wind: chesed, gevura and the middle, tiferes; their initials spell omer
the breath of the heart: the lungs, and inside it the spiritual breath, the emotion
a voice sweet to the soul: a blend of joy and sadness
blending, the mix of the emotions in the heart
running and returning: the beat of all life, the heart, the breath, the brain
the voice that is heard: the emotion you can hear in speech
the speaking wind: literally a wind, pushed by the lungs through the windpipe
the letters of thought, Leah; happy, angry or sad letters
too weary to contain: why thought is called Leah, always overfilled
the musings of the heart: passing thoughts the outer middos raise

sections.title: Leah and Rachel are thought and speech; first, the voice of Yaakov
sections.summary: The chapter will explain how Yisroel and Yaakov, the *middos*, unite with Leah and Rachel, thought and speech. First a preface on *Zeir Anpin*: the voice comes from it, and there is a voice that is heard and a voice that is not.

phrases.he: (לז) ומעתה יש להבין בענין יחוד דישראל ויעקב בלאה ורחל.
וביאור ענין לאה ורחל ידוע, שזהו ענין מחשבה ודבור
והיינו ענין ב' ההי''ן דשם יהו״ה כמו שכתוב בזהר, תרין נוקבין פריש שלמה כו'
אתי מלבנון כלה כו'
ה' ראשונה שם הגדולה לאה, וה' אחרונה שם הקטנה רחל כו'
ותחילה יש להקדים
phrases.en: Before we get to *yichudei Zu"n*, we're going to be *makdim* something in terms of *Zeir Anpin*.

phrases.he: בענין הקול קול יעקב,
phrases.en: that the voice is the voice of Yaakov, that the voice comes from *Zeir Anpin*

phrases.he: שיש קלה פנימאה דלא משתמע כו'
phrases.en: There's a voice that's heard and a voice that's not heard.

blocks.text: The chapter sets out to explain the union of Yisroel and Yaakov with Leah and Rachel, which are thought and speech, the two *heis* of the Name *Havaya*. By the way, Leah is called here the upper *hei*, and the upper *hei* is really *bina*. Leah should really be part of the lower *hei*, since the outer side of thought is also called *Malchus*. The whole subject here, Yisroel and Leah, is *Zeir Anpin* (lit. the small countenance) and *Nukva* (lit. the female), and *Nukva* is *Malchus*, not *bina*.

Thought has different levels, as came up on chapter 2, and they work together: its *chitzoniyus* (outer side) is the letters themselves, its *pnimiyus* (inner side) the actual intellect of the thought.

The unions of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva* come later. First a preface about *Zeir Anpin*: **the voice is the voice of Yaakov**, the voice comes from *Zeir Anpin*, and there is a voice that is heard and a voice that is not. In speech, the voice itself comes from the lungs and the heart, while its cutting into letters comes from *bina*, and goes from *bina* to Leah to Rachel: the letters are split up in thought, and from there go into speech. That is what the next few chapters are about. First, the voice and its two kinds.

sections.title: The voice that is heard: fire, water and wind in the breath of the heart
sections.summary: The breath of the heart is made of spiritual fire, water and wind, *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*, and they show in the voice: a hoarse voice from fire, a clear one from water. The most beautiful voice is a blend of joy and sadness, and that depends on the heart, not on training.

phrases.he: להיות ידוע בענין יום ליום יביע אמר,
phrases.en: From one day to another day he'll give *omer*.

phrases.he: שזהו אש מים רוח חג''ת
כמו הקול שהוא מורכב מאש מים רוח הגשמיים, כך הבל הלב עצמו כלול מאש מים רוח רוחניים
שהוא בחינת חסד וגבורה והממוצע שהוא הרוח
phrases.en: The *memutza* means *tiferes*, which is *ruach*.

phrases.he: דהיינו בחינת כיווץ והתפשטות שבהבל הרוחני דלב

blocks.text: "Day to day utters speech (*omer*)": *omer* is the initials of *esh mayim ruach* (fire, water, wind), which are *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*. As the physical voice is made of physical elements, the *hevel halev* (breath of the heart) itself is made of spiritual fire, water and wind: *chesed* and *gevura*, and the middle, *tiferes*, which is *ruach*. This is the contracting and expanding in the spiritual breath of the heart.

phrases.he: כמו כאשר האדם שמח בלבו, אז יש בחינת אור ההתפשטות בלב,
phrases.en: Then his heart like opens up big.

phrases.he: והוא הבל דחסדים
phrases.en: and that's called the *hevel d'chasadim*

phrases.he: וכשהוא בעוצב, הוא בבחינת הכיווץ וצמצום,
phrases.en: he feels like his heart is *farkvetched*

phrases.he: והוא בחינת הבל דגבורות
והממוצע מחסד וגבורה הוא הבל רוחני, ממוצע ממוזג
מאמצעות חסד וגבורה
כרוח הממוצע מאש ומים בגשם ההבל
phrases.en: like the *ruach*, which is a *memutza* from fire and water

blocks.text: When a person is happy, his heart **opens up big**: that is the *hevel d'chasadim*, the breath of kindness. When he is sad, **he feels like his heart is *farkvetched*** (squeezed): the *hevel d'gevuros*. The middle is a breath of both together, **like the *ruach*, which is a *memutza* from fire and water**.

phrases.he: כידוע שהצמאון מיסוד האש
phrases.en: that thirst comes from fire

phrases.he: וכן ניחר גרוני כו'
phrases.en: my throat is like scratchy

phrases.he: בקול הגשמי, בא מתגבורת יסוד אש שבהבל הלב
phrases.en: a voice that comes from fire, that's like a hoarse voice

phrases.he: ולהיפך צלילת קול הבל הלב מיסוד המים כו'
phrases.en: a voice that's like a bell, very clear voice, from *yesod hamayim*

phrases.he: והממוצע שהוא רוח ממוזג כו'
phrases.en: and the middle, which is like a more spiritual voice

blocks.text: Thirst comes from fire, and so does a hoarse voice, **my throat is like scratchy**: the strength of the fire in the breath of the heart, a voice like Louis Armstrong's. The opposite, a voice clear as a bell, comes from water. The middle is a more spiritual voice. A really good voice has both together: not totally hoarse, and not totally like a bell, which is beautiful but only good for certain things. The real good singers have a little mixture of both.

phrases.he: וכך הוא בקול הממוצע וממוזג מחדוה ומרירות ועוצב,
שנקרא קול ערב לנפש,
phrases.en: That's what's called a beautiful voice, that it's beautiful to listen to.

phrases.he: שזה תלוי במזיגה הרוחנית שבהבל הלב דוקא כו'
phrases.en: The beautiful voice depends on the *mezigah* in the heart.

blocks.text: Besides the tone there is the emotion of the voice. A voice blended of joy, bitterness and sadness is called *kol arev lanefesh*, **a beautiful voice, that it's beautiful to listen to**. The greatest singers, the big cantors, have a mixture of happiness and sadness in their voices. A totally crying voice is not beautiful: it is missing the clarity. Just a happy voice, like kids playing and shouting, is not beautiful either. A cantor has the clarity of a happy voice and that crying quality too; so does opera. **The beautiful voice depends on the *mezigah* in the heart**, the blend of its emotions.
So voice training is not enough to make a great singer, even with a good voice to start with. The real thing about a great singer is that he can put feeling into his voice.

blocks.title: Shlomo Carlebach and Bob Dylan
blocks.text: Some very famous singers really don't have a good voice, or the training either. Two examples: Shlomo Carlebach, *alav hashalom*, and, *l'havdil*, Bob Dylan. In the Jewish song market Carlebach is probably the biggest superstar, more than Mordechai Ben David or anybody like that, though some of them have a much better voice; his was not all that great, and sometimes a little off-key. But he could really get the feeling into the song, so people loved to hear it. The same with Bob Dylan: no great voice, no real training, but he conveys a real feeling in the song.

sensitivity.reason: Says the voice of a recent, named singer was not great and sometimes off-key, and that a living one has no great voice or training.
sensitivity.publishable: Some very famous singers really don't have a good voice, or the training either. Two examples: Shlomo Carlebach, *alav hashalom*, and, *l'havdil*, Bob Dylan. In the Jewish song market Carlebach is probably the biggest superstar, more than Mordechai Ben David or anybody like that, though some of them have a much better voice. But he could really get the feeling into the song, so people loved to hear it. The same with Bob Dylan: he conveys a real feeling in the song.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: The remark on their voices is mild, affectionate, and is the point of the example (feeling, not voice); it may well print as said.

blocks.title: Pure technique and no feeling
blocks.text: Even among operatic voices, the difference between a good voice and a real superstar like Pavarotti is that he can get an emotion across. It is heart to heart, not just lungs and larynx. That is why the great singers close their eyes when they sing and concentrate, going in a little: it is not just technique. Someone with a fantastic voice and fantastic technique and no feeling sings it perfectly, and it is boring. You can hear the feeling in the voice; that is what the text is saying.

The sweetness of the voice depends *davka* (precisely) on the breath of the heart. The *hevel halev* here is the lungs, by the way; but the inner side of the breath of the heart is the spiritual breath in the heart itself: the emotion.

sections.title: Life runs and returns: the beat of the heart, the breath and the brain
sections.summary: The life-spirit in the heart beats, contracting and expanding, and all life goes in beats, *ratzo v'shov*. The heart contracts when it receives from the brain, the opposite of the blood. The same beat is in the brain and in music.

phrases.he: וגם ברוח החיים שבחלל הימיני וחלל השמאלי, הרי הוא בבחינת רצוא ושוב בדפיקו דלבא,
phrases.en: The whole life force in the heart, in a way of *ratzo v'shov*, in the beating of the heart

phrases.he: כידוע שזהו גם כן בבחינת כיווץ והתפשטות
phrases.en: The whole thing of the beating of the heart that keeps you alive is that it kvetches and opens, and kvetches and opens.

phrases.he: (אלא שהוא בהיפך,
phrases.en: except it's opposite

phrases.he: כאשר רוח החיים נכנס מן המוח בלב מתקווץ לקבל וכשיוצא מתפשט כו'(
phrases.en: When the *ruach chaim* comes from the *moach* into the heart, the message the brain sends into the heart, then it's *miskavetz*; and when it goes away, then it's *mispashet*.

phrases.he: לפי שהחיות דוקא רצוא ושוב כו'
phrases.en: The whole thing of *chayus* is all *ratzo v'shov*.

phrases.he: וכמבואר בספרי הרפואה)
phrases.en: And this is explained in medical books, that everything goes with beats.

blocks.text: The life-spirit in the right and left chambers of the heart is *ratzo v'shov* (running and returning) in the heart's beat, again contracting and expanding: **the whole thing of the beating of the heart that keeps you alive is that it kvetches and opens, and kvetches and opens**.

**Except it's opposite**: when the life-spirit comes from the brain into the heart, the heart contracts to receive, and when it leaves, the heart expands. What is he talking about? Ask the physicians why the heart kvetches: it receives a message from the brain through the nerves, and like any muscle it kvetches when it gets the message. So it receives from the brain when it contracts, not when it expands. With the blood it is just the opposite: when the heart kvetches the blood is sent out, and when it expands the blood is taken in.

"For the *chayus* (life) is *davka* running and returning" is a pun: it is said that the *Chayos* above run back and forth, and the *chayus* of a person goes the same way. **The whole thing of *chayus* is all *ratzo v'shov***.

blocks.title: The beats of the brain
blocks.text: Breathing goes in and out, the heart beats, the whole blood system works that way, and the life force from the brain into the nerves also goes in beats. With biofeedback they now know the brain's different beats, theta and delta: light sleep is theta, deep sleep delta, so many beats a second. As the heart is faster when we are active and slows when we sleep, so the brain's beats slow down: awake they go up to something like ten a second (he can't remember the number), and at four or lower it is deep sleep. The whole *chayus* is in and out: beats.

blocks.title: A slow sad song and a polka
blocks.text: That is also why music, rhythm, singing and life are all tied together. A slow, sad song with a slow rhythm makes people sad, even cry; a fast song like a polka or rock and roll gets you going; songs can even get you mad. It is because life runs and returns, as the medical books explain: everything goes with beats.

sections.title: From the heart to the mouth: the voice that is heard, and the speaking wind
sections.summary: The emotion that can be heard in speech is the union of Yaakov and Rachel. The power of speech is a wind pushed by the lungs through a reed, and the emotions move the bellows, so the voice carries them. Speech itself depends on the heart: a sad man does not want to talk, a happy one tells everybody.

phrases.he: וכל זה נקרא קלא דמשתמע בדבור,
phrases.en: And this part here is called the voice that is heard.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת רוח הבל הדבור
והיינו בחינת קול ודבור הנזכר בזהר בכמה דוכתי
והוא בחינת יחוד יעקב ורחל
דהיינו בחינת ההמשכה של המדות שבלב הבא בבחינת רוח הבל הלב, מורכב מאש מים רוח רוחניים, עד בחינת קול הדבור
phrases.en: *hamshacha* of the *middos* into the voice, as *murkav* from *chomer ruchani*

blocks.text: All this is called *kala d'mishtama*, **the voice that is heard**: the emotion you can hear in speech, the breath of the voice of speech. Animals have it too: in a dog's voice you can hear if he is happy or sad. This is the voice and speech the *Zohar* speaks of, the union of Yaakov and Rachel: the drawing of the heart's *middos* (emotional attributes) through the breath of the heart until the voice of speech.

blocks.title: "Oh, nothing"
blocks.text: Listening to someone talk, you hear not only the words but the emotions. A man comes home and asks his wife what's the matter, and she insists nothing is the matter. From the voice you can tell it is not nothing: it is a crying voice. Going by the words alone he would say, "That's nice, I'm glad you're happy."

sensitivity.reason: A stock scene of a wife who says "nothing" is the matter in a crying voice.
sensitivity.publishable: Listening to someone talk, you hear not only the words but the emotions. Someone asks a person close to him what's the matter, and the answer is that nothing is the matter. From the voice you can tell it is not nothing: it is a crying voice. Going by the words alone he would say, "That's nice, I'm glad you're happy."
sensitivity.judgmentNote: An ordinary household scene, not a claim about women; the point (emotion heard in the voice) is the same either way, and it may print as said.

blocks.text: That is "the voice is the voice of Yaakov": the emotion goes into the voice to connect with the actual speech. This is *kala d'mishtama*, the *hamshacha* (drawing down) **of the *middos* into the voice**.

phrases.he: ובחינת כח הדבור נמשך מנקב החזה דלב כו'
phrases.en: And the power of speaking comes from the *nekev hechaze d'lev*, the hole: there's a hole at the end of the lungs.

phrases.he: ונקרא רוח ממללא
phrases.en: It's called a talking wind, and it's literally a wind, literally.

blocks.text: At the voice of speech it becomes made of physical matter: a physical voice, yet in it you can hear *chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*. The power of speech comes from "the hole of the chest": **there's a hole at the end of the lungs**, then a tube, the windpipe, and that is how you can talk. The lungs have to push the air out to make a voice. So it is called *ruach memalela*, **a talking wind, and it's literally a wind**. We don't mean spirit.

blocks.title: A wind instrument
blocks.text: The lungs are like a bellows pushing a wind through the windpipe, and the larynx is something like an oboe: the voice is basically a wind instrument, and like an oboe, if you don't blow into it, it makes no noise. Or like the noisemakers at parties: you blow, it goes toot, and the thing shoots out like a frog's tongue, with a little reed in it like a harmonica's. The voice is slightly more sophisticated. A harmonica reed does one thing; this reed stretches and reshapes itself, so you can sing all in one reed, like stretching the end of a blown-up balloon to make different noises.

So there is a flexible reed you can stretch, and a bellows that is not fixed: it can push out more air or less, and the way it pushes is affected by the emotions in the heart. So the voice that finally comes through the reed is one in which you can actually hear the emotion.

blocks.title: Interested or bored
blocks.text: Even in speaking you can hear whether someone really means it, or is really interested in what he is saying. Listen to the voice in this class: it sounds interested in the lesson, not bored, "wow wow, wa-ba-ba-wow-wow". Someone else says the same words, and it doesn't sound like he's into it.

blocks.title: "You don't sound sorry"
blocks.text: Besides *chesed* and *gevura*, you can hear *netzach* (victory) and *hod* too. Tell a guy to say uncle, or tell a little kid to say sorry: he says sorry, and you tell him he doesn't sound sorry. "I just said sorry!" You did not hear the *hod* in his voice: he is not really *modeh* (admitting) that you are right and he is wrong.
That is *ruach memalela*. The power to talk comes from the lungs: without the bellows pushing, you could not talk.

phrases.he: (והיינו מה שכתוב בעץ חיים
דכתר דנוקבא דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: the beginning of the speech

phrases.he: דבוק בחזה דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: is connected to the lungs

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב לעולם יהו״ה דברך נצב בשמים כו'
phrases.en: The *Malchus* is *nitzav* in the *esh* and *mayim* of the heart.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ממצוא חפצך ודבר דבר, מקור כח הדבור שנמשך מהבל הלב דזעיר אנפין

blocks.text: So *Etz Chaim* says the *Keser* of the *Nukva* of *Zeir Anpin* is attached to the chest of *Zeir Anpin*: **the beginning of the speech** is connected to the lungs. "Forever, G-d, Your word stands in the heavens": **the *Malchus* is *nitzav* in the *esh* and *mayim* of the heart**, it stands in its fire and water. And on *Shabbos* one refrains from "speaking words" of weekday business: not only not to say them, but it should stop even in the heart, where the power of speech comes from.

phrases.he: וכנראה בחוש, שאם הלב עצב בכיווץ ימעיט בדבור,
phrases.en: you see that if a person is real sad, then he doesn't want to talk

phrases.he: וכשהוא בהתפשטות ירחיב הדבור
phrases.en: and when a person is real happy, then he wants to talk

phrases.he: לפי שכח של הדבור תלוי בהבל הקול שבלב עצמו כו')
phrases.en: because the power of speech really comes from the heart

blocks.text: You see it plainly: a person who is really sad doesn't want to talk. He just wants to sit there and mope; you say "Come on, talk to me," and he doesn't want to. When a person is really happy he wants to talk, to tell everybody about it. **Because the power of speech really comes from the heart**: the *Keser* of *Malchus* comes from *Zeir Anpin*, the emotions, and their expansion makes a will to talk, or a will not to.

sections.title: Said, not only felt: the king's word, and free choice
sections.summary: What stays in the heart is not yet the king's word; once spoken, it must be done. So it is said of a person before birth everything but whether he will be righteous or wicked: that is only thought, which leaves choice open. In the heart of *Zeir Anpin* things can still turn from *din* to *chesed*.

phrases.he: וכאשר לא נמשך מהבל הלב בדבור, על דרך שאמר לבא לפומא לא גליא,
phrases.en: If he doesn't say what he has in his heart into his mouth, means he just keeps it in his heart: the heart does not reveal it to the mouth.

phrases.he: לא נעשה דבר מלך עדיין
phrases.en: then you cannot have a command of the king

phrases.he: מאין ליש כלל
phrases.en: It doesn't become a something.

phrases.he: וכמו ואילו צדיק ורשע לא קאמר
phrases.en: But *tzaddik v'rasha*, it doesn't say.

phrases.he: כי בדבור כבר נעשה, כי הוא אמר ויהי,
phrases.en: Once He says, it has to be like this.

phrases.he: וכן ודברי אשר יצא מפי לא ישוב ריקם כו'
phrases.en: Once I say something, it has to happen.

blocks.text: When the heart does not reveal it to the mouth and he just keeps it in his heart, it has not yet become a word of the king. The king cannot complain that he wanted something in his heart and they did the opposite; he cannot call it rebellion against the kingdom. "When did you say it, king?" "Well, I didn't say it, but I felt it." That he can't do. Unspoken, **it doesn't become a something**, so it does not have to be done.

Forty days before a person is born, just about everything about him is said: whom he will marry, where he will live. **But *tzaddik v'rasha*, it doesn't say**, righteous or wicked. He thinks it and does not say it; had He said it, there could be no *teshuva* (return). Then how were Yaakov and Esav so before birth? Here the tape turns over.

blocks.question: If Yaakov and Esav were already so before they were born, why blame Esav, or praise Yaakov?
blocks.text: A person is born with a predisposition to be a *tzaddik* or a *rasha*, as with Yaakov and Esav, because He did think it. But He did not say it. Yaakov could have been affected by the world and become, *chas v'shalom*, a *rasha*, and Esav could have done *teshuva*; had he done it, he could have been even bigger than Yaakov.
blocks.outOfPlace: Class 207 opens by finishing the question on line 33 that class 206 broke off at the turn of the tape; it rereads lines 33-34 at w412.

blocks.title: Why Yitzchak loved Esav
blocks.text: That is why Yitzchak loved him more. On the outside, he was fooled. The more internal meaning: he loved him because in thought he was a *rasha*. A listener says he saw his potential; yes, but the potential was there because in thought he was a *rasha*. Esav fooled him into thinking he was a *tzaddik*, as Rashi says, asking how to tithe salt and straw. Still, Yaakov was a *tzaddik* too, and the *Avos* (the Patriarchs) do not love someone on a whim. The reason: one who was a *rasha* in thought and became a *tzaddik* is even bigger than Yaakov, for whom being a *tzaddik* was no big deal, since in thought he was already one.
blocks.outOfPlace: The end of class 207's opening on line 33, before it rereads lines 33-34 at w412.

blocks.text: He did not say *tzaddik* or *rasha*: had He said it, there would be no free choice. For in speech it is already done, "He said and it was": **once He says, it has to be like this**. And "My word that goes out of My mouth shall not return empty": **once I say something, it has to happen**.

phrases.he: אבל בלב דזעיר אנפין עדיין יכול להתהפך מדין לחסד,
כמו וינחם יהו״ה כו'
phrases.en: The *Aibershter* changed His mind.

phrases.he: וכן ויאמר אל לבו
phrases.en: He said to His heart

phrases.he: לא אוסיף עוד כו'
וזהו בחינת חג''ת דהבל הלב דזעיר אנפין שבא ומתייחד בדבור, עלמא דאתגליא כו' כידוע ודי למבין.

blocks.text: But in the heart of *Zeir Anpin* it can still turn from *din* (judgement) to *chesed*: "and G-d regretted", the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d) **changed His mind**; "He said to His heart, I will not again...". This is the *Chagas* (*chesed*, *gevura* and *tiferes*) of the breath of the heart of *Zeir Anpin* coming into speech, the revealed world. That is *kala d'mishtama*, the actual voice in which you hear the emotions; next comes the voice that is not heard.

sections.title: The inner voice that is not heard: Yisroel and Leah
sections.summary: Within the emotion is its reason, the *mochin*, which you cannot hear in the voice: you hear that he is angry, not why. Through *daas* it goes right away into the letters of thought, Leah, which receive them from *Malchus* of *tevuna*. Thought keeps the emotion alive, so changing the thought can break it.

phrases.he: ויש בחינת קלא פנימאה דלא משתמע בדבור כלל, והוא בחינת המוחין שבמדות חסד וגבורה
כמו אהבה ויראה שלמעלה מבחינת רוח החיים שבלב, כמו עצם חדוה של אהבה וחסד או עצם רוגז ודין של יראה ופחד
שהמה רוחניים הרבה גם מהרכבת הרוחניות דאש מים רוח הנזכר לעיל, הבא במורכב בלב הגשמי
וגם שיש בזה הרכבה מאש מים רוח, שהוא בחינת חסד גבורה ותפארת, אבל הוא בבחינת הפנימית שבלב
שהוא במדות חג''ת, שיש בהן הארת המוחין הנקרא קלא פנימאה דבינה שבזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: in other words, the actual reason

phrases.he: הבא ונמשך מן המוח ללב

blocks.text: There is also a *kala pnima'a* (inner voice) not heard in speech at all: the *mochin* (lit. brains; the intellect) within *chesed* and *gevura*, the love and fear above the life-spirit in the heart, the essential joy of love or the essential anger of fear. They are far more spiritual than the fire, water and wind in the physical heart: the inner side of the heart, lit by the *mochin*, the inner voice of *bina* in *Zeir Anpin*. **In other words, the actual reason.**

blocks.title: Mad, but at whom?
blocks.text: From the voice you can tell someone is sad, but not why. You can see the guy is mad, but you don't know why, or who he is mad at; or why he is happy, and with what. Did he make some money? Win the lottery? Meet a good friend? That inner voice of *bina*, which comes from the brain to the heart, you can't hear.

phrases.he: וכאשר הוא בא בהתפעלות רוחניות שעל ידי הדעת,
בחינת ישראל הנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: which is called Yisroel

phrases.he: ונמשך מיד באותיות המחשבה
phrases.en: and right away it becomes *osios hamachshava*, that he thinks why he's mad

phrases.he: שנקרא לאה,
phrases.en: and that's called Leah

phrases.he: נקרא יחוד ישראל ולאה
פנימיות המדות שבלב
מיד מהרהר במחשבה
phrases.en: Right away, it's *meharher bemachshava*.

phrases.he: אם מתפעל בשכל וטעם לאהבה וחסד,
הרי מיד יבוא מדה זו עם המוחין שבה במחשבה
phrases.en: It's this *midda* with the *mochin* comes into the *machshava*.

blocks.text: When it comes as a spiritual stirring through *daas* (knowledge), Yisroel, and is drawn right away into the letters of thought, Leah, that is the union of Yisroel and Leah. This inner reasoning comes from the inner part of the emotion, *daas*, which is also emotion but the *sechel* (intellect) of it, **which is called Yisroel**; **right away it becomes *osios hamachshava*** (the letters of thought): he thinks why he's mad. "You hit me." And that thought you can't hear in the voice.

If he is stirred by reason to love and kindness, the *midda* (attribute) comes right away with its *mochin* into thought. Thought is only letters, but there are different kinds: happy letters, angry letters, sad letters. The letters of a thought that holds the reason of a *midda* are not dead letters; they have a quality to them.

phrases.he: וכידוע שהמחשבה מלבשת המדות דישראל בפרטיהם
ונקרא לאה, כמו נלאה להכיל המדות כו',
phrases.en: it's too much for her to contain the *middos*

phrases.he: ושרש לאה למעלה בבינה
phrases.en: And the *shoresh* of Leah is upstairs in *bina*.

phrases.he: היינו לאה ילדה ששה בנים,
phrases.en: Leah gave birth to six children

phrases.he: בחינת ו׳ קצוות דמדות דזעיר אנפין
phrases.en: That is the *middos* from *chesed* to *yesod*.

phrases.he: אך יחוד ישראל ולאה, היינו מוחין דאבא ואמא שבזעיר אנפין,
phrases.en: the *yichud* of Yisroel and Leah, that is the *mochin* of *Abba*, means of the *sechel*, which is in *Zeir Anpin*, the actual reason for the emotion

phrases.he: הוא מתייחד בלאה התחתונה,
phrases.en: not in the upper Leah, which is *bina*, the *shoresh* of Leah, but in the actual *machshava*, in the *osios* of the *machshava*

phrases.he: דמחשבה שמקבלת מבחינת מלכות דתבונה, שרש המחשבה כו' ודי למבין.
phrases.en: The *machshava*, even though it becomes a *levush* for *Zeir Anpin*, really receives from *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

blocks.text: Thought dresses Yisroel's *middos* in their particulars and is called Leah, from *nil'ah lehachil* (too weary to contain): **it's too much for her to contain the *middos***. Thought is always overfilled, so a person can never stop thinking; and when he is really happy, sad or angry, he can hardly think at all: "my brain is blowing up, I'm so angry at the guy". Leah's root is in *bina*, so the two are sometimes named almost interchangeably.

**Leah gave birth to six children**, the six extremities of the *middos* of *Zeir Anpin*, from *chesed* to *yesod*. The union of Yisroel and Leah is the *mochin* of *Abba* (lit. father; *chachma*), the reason for the emotion, uniting not with the upper Leah, which is *bina*, but with the lower one: the letters of thought. Thought, though it becomes a garment for *Zeir Anpin*, receives its letters from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, the root of thought; that is the inner voice that is not heard, the voice of the intellect. The *midda* too really receives from the same place, *Malchus* of *tevuna*, through *daas*.

blocks.title: Count to ten; whistle a happy tune
blocks.text: It receives through thought: the thought gives the *midda* its life force, so that without the thought the *midda* can die. That is the reason for counting to ten. When someone is really mad, they tell him to count to ten; when someone is scared, there is the song "Whistle a Happy Tune". Forcing a different thought, different letters in your head, breaks the thought that clothes and holds the anger, the inner voice of the anger. The *midda* has no *kli* (vessel), and it sort of disappears.

blocks.title: A lion in the room
blocks.text: Of course, if a lion is standing in the room with you, it will be very hard to whistle a happy tune. The *midda* is getting directly from the brain: *bina* keeps putting into the thought, "Hey, the lion is still here." If you can really whistle a happy tune with a lion there, and literally stop thinking about it, you will stop being scared. That is very hard to do. Not only that: scared or not, the lion might kill him.

Sometimes it is good to whistle a happy tune: where it is not a real lion, like walking in the dark, a phobia. Where there is a real lion, even walking at night in a dangerous part of town, listen to your phobia instead and do something about it. That too is a *tikkun* (repair): knowing when to whistle a happy tune and when to listen to the phobia. Most of the time, listen to the phobia first and see if there is a real thing behind it.

sensitivity.reason: Advice on handling fears and phobias (listen to the phobia first) that a reader might act on.
sensitivity.publishable: Sometimes it is good to whistle a happy tune: where it is not a real lion. Where there is a real lion, do something about it. That too is a *tikkun* (repair): knowing when to whistle a happy tune and when to listen to the fear.
sensitivity.judgmentNote: Practical psychological advice in his own name; it is common sense and may print as said, but it is the kind of remark a reader acts on.

blocks.title: Escapist movies
blocks.text: Much of what people are into comes from this. In depressions and wars, movies become very popular: escapist movies get people's heads off their problems. At a comedy they laugh, and while they laugh they are actually happy, since the thought is about the movie and not about their situation. That is why people drink and take drugs, or go to a bar and talk with other people, or go to the football game.

Who cares who won the football game, or whom they will hire for next season? A lot of the people who talk about all that would get depressed if they thought about their own problems, so they think about the football game instead. That is also why women like to watch all these soap operas: it gets them off their own problems.

sensitivity.reason: Sneers at sports fans as people avoiding their own problems, and says women watch soap operas to escape theirs.
sensitivity.publishable: A lot of the people who talk about who won the football game would get depressed if they thought about their own problems, so they think about the football game instead. That is also why people like to watch all these soap operas: it gets them off their own problems.

blocks.text: All this is because thought holds the *midda*: the union of Yisroel and Leah. And though thought clothes a *midda*, its letters really come from *Malchus* of *tevuna*, the real root of thought.

sections.title: Four unions, and the order of the flow
sections.summary: Yisroel, the inner *middos*, and Yaakov, the outer, each unite with Leah, thought, and with Rachel, speech. Usually the feeling rises into thought, comes back to the breath of the heart and out in speech; sometimes thought goes straight into speech. Either way there is no thought without *middos*.

phrases.he: ויש יחוד ישראל ורחל, כאשר בא הארת בחינת פנימיות המוחין שבמדות בדבור
phrases.en: when the *mochin* come directly into *dibur*

blocks.text: There is a union of Yisroel and Rachel, **when the *mochin* come directly into *dibur*** (speech): he talks straight out of his brain. That is very uncommon; it is hard even to give an example, except someone saying over *Chassidus* so totally into it that he says it almost without going through a real thought. Even then there has to be a Leah, since you cannot talk without thinking; the connection is just so direct that the Leah is negligible, totally transparent.

phrases.he: וכן יש יחוד יעקב ולאה, שנקרא הרהורי לבא, דהיינו מה שבבחינת חיצוניות המדות עולה בהרהור במוח
וכן יש יחוד יעקב ורחל שהוא המשכת חיצוניות המדות שבלב בדבור כנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: When the *chitzoniyus hamiddos* in the *lev* go into *dibur*

blocks.text: The union of Yaakov and Leah is called *hirhurei liba* (the musings of the heart): what the outer *middos* raise in the mind. He thinks, "Oh, that car I liked." It is not the inner side of a *midda*, like fear of a lion, but something he likes or doesn't like, or something that happened at work: just regular stuff from the outer heart coming up as thoughts in his head as he walks down the street.

And the union of Yaakov and Rachel is **when the *chitzoniyus hamiddos* in the *lev* go into *dibur***, the outer *middos* of the heart drawn into speech. There too a thought is always in the middle; it just doesn't count.

phrases.he: וסדר ההמשכה לפעמים כך הוא,
phrases.en: and it works in different ways

phrases.he: שבחינת המדות שבלב עולה ומתייחד במחשבה
phrases.en: he has a *midda* in his heart that goes up and is *misyached* in the *machshava*

phrases.he: ומן המחשבה בא אל הלב,
phrases.en: and from the *machshava* it comes

phrases.he: בחיצוניות הבל הלב,
phrases.en: to the *chitzoniyus* of the heart, means into the lungs

phrases.he: ומהבל הלב נכנס להבל הדבור שנקרא קול ודבור
ולפעמים מן המחשבה נכנס אל הדבור, וכמו שמדבר מה שחושב
phrases.en: In other words, he says what he thinks.

phrases.he: שעקבי לאה נכנסין תוך ראש רחל כו'
phrases.en: the feet of Leah go inside the head of Rachel

phrases.he: ובשעה זו שמדבר מה שחושב,
phrases.en: and at this time when he talks what he thinks

phrases.he: הרי יוצא מקול הבל הלב בדבור בה' מוצאות
ובודאי מה שבלבו עולה במחשבה,
phrases.en: but even then it has to be what's in his heart, it goes up in *machshava*

phrases.he: שאין מחשבה בלא מדות שבלב כו'
phrases.en: you can't have a *machshava* without *middos*

phrases.he: ונמצא בחינת יעקב, שהוא רוח הבל קול הלב, משמש במחשבה ודבור שנקרא ב' אחיות, לאה ורחל
עלמא דאתכסיא ועלמא דאתגליא, מאמר סתום ומאמר פתוח כידוע ודי למבין

blocks.text: The order of the flow varies. Sometimes **he has a *midda* in his heart that goes up and is *misyached* in the *machshava***, unites with thought: he has to think about it. From the thought it comes back **to the *chitzoniyus* of the heart, means into the lungs**, and from the breath of the heart into the breath of speech, called voice and speech. This is the usual way.
Sometimes it goes from thought straight into speech: **he says what he thinks**. As they say, a smart guy thinks what he says, and a *meshuga* says what he thinks.

sensitivity.reason: The saying calls the one who says what he thinks a meshuga (a madman).
sensitivity.publishable: Sometimes it goes from thought straight into speech: **he says what he thinks**. As they say, a smart guy thinks what he says.

blocks.text: When he thinks of something and right away says it, **the feet of Leah go inside the head of Rachel**, like in a Kung Fu movie. At this time the voice of the breath of the heart comes out in speech through the five places of articulation.

But even then what is in his heart goes up into thought: **you can't have a *machshava* without *middos***, even a thought of pure intellect. Reading out of a book, as in this class, there has to be a *midda* in the heart that wants to learn it: some *netzach* and *hod*, love for the thing and hatred of anything that would stop it. Without *middos* there would not even be the *netzach* to come up and talk. Someone giving an intellectual speech is not a robot: there is a power in it, an emotion, and you can hear it in his voice.

So Yaakov, the breath of the voice of the heart, serves thought and speech, the two sisters Leah and Rachel: the hidden world and the revealed world, the closed saying and the open one, thought and speech.

sections.title: Speaking from Yisroel: the inner unions, and Shabbos
sections.summary: The same unions happen in the inner *middos*: the reason itself goes into thought and speech. You cannot hear it in the voice, only in the letters, as "there is no speech and no words". A class like this one is such a union, holiness coming into speech, like *Shabbos*.

phrases.he: (ועל דרך זה
phrases.en: in the same way

phrases.he: יש יחוד ישראל ולאה ויחוד ישראל ורחל בפנימיות המדות, בבחינת קלא פנימאה הנזכר לעיל
וזה שכתוב יביע אמ״ר,
phrases.en: it will give out the *esh*, *mayim* and *ruach*

phrases.he: ואחר כך, אין אומר, במחשבה, ואין דברים
phrases.en: There is this *omer* and things, you can't hear them in the voice.

phrases.he: והיינו בשבת שהיחוד בפנימיות דזעיר אנפין ונוקבא כו' כידוע ומבואר הכל במקום אחר ודי למבין):

blocks.text: **In the same way** there are unions of Yisroel with Leah and with Rachel in the inner side of the *middos*, the inner voice. From the inner *middos* it goes to thought, from thought back to the outer breath, and from there to Rachel. Or he speaks what he thinks; but even then Yisroel has to be there.

Talking about a deep intellectual thing, as in this class, the union going into speech and thought is *davka* from Yisroel, not from Yaakov: not emotional things but the real inner Yisroel, a thought of the intellect. That is what becomes one with thought and speech. This is the inner voice: you can't hear it in the voice itself, but you can hear it in the letters.

So "[day to day] utters speech (*omer*)": **it will give out the *esh*, *mayim* and *ruach***, the *middos*, in the voice. Then it says "there is no speech and there are no words": an inner thing you can't hear in the voice, though you can hear it in the letters, which come out of *Malchus* of *tevuna*.

blocks.title: You can hear that he is interested, not what he says
blocks.text: Whoever hears his voice now knows he is talking about something he is really interested in and connected to. But what he is talking about you can't hear from the voice. Someone who doesn't understand English, or understands the words but isn't up to where the class is, can hear the words and still not understand: that is *davka* in the letters.

Later the text will explain how everything can come into *Malchus*, even the intellect and even the *Keser* (crown), as in "*Keser Malchus*". On *Shabbos* the union is in the inner side of *Zeir Anpin* and *Nukva*: holiness. What this class is doing is like *Shabbos*, a union of holiness into speech.

reviewQuestions.question: What makes a voice hoarse, what makes it clear, and what makes it *kol arev lanefesh*?
Why does the heart contract when the life-spirit comes into it from the brain, and what does "*chayus* is *ratzo v'shov*" mean?
How does the emotion of the heart get into the sound of speech, and why is a sad person short of words?
Why is a thing only felt in the heart not yet "the word of the king", and what does that have to do with free choice?
What can you hear in a person's voice and what can't you, and how does counting to ten break anger?
What are the four unions of Yisroel and Yaakov with Leah and Rachel, and in what order does the flow usually go?

notes.text: Lines 33-34 are read in both classes: 206 reads them at the end of the side (w3750-3811) and 207 rereads them (w412-452). Line 33's English is from 206 (w3794-3799), the only place it is rendered; line 34's from 207 (w436-460), since 206 reads it without translating. 207 opens (w1-411) by finishing the question 206 broke off at the turn of the tape (why Yaakov and Esav were so before birth); those two blocks sit under lines 32-34 with outOfPlace.

He reads line 3's Zohar quotation differently from the chapter file (206 w23-39: "תרין נוקבין תרין שלימין, כולהו אחידין בלבנא"), and line 7 as "מהאברים הגשמיים / הרוחניים" (w450-462) for "מאש מים רוח הגשמיים / רוחניים"; possibly the transcript. He does not translate either line; the block follows the chapter's text.

His remark on the text (206 w88-161): the line calls Leah the upper hei (bina), but Leah should really be the lower hei, since Yisroel and Leah here are Zeir Anpin and Nukva, and Nukva is Malchus. Kept in the first block as his comment. He also refers back to a question raised "in chapter 2" by a student (named in the class; written without the name).

His physiology (206 w1577-1783): the heart contracts because it receives a message from the brain through the nerves. In fact the heartbeat starts in the heart's own pacemaker and the nerves only change its rate; not flagged, since it explains the line, but a reviewer may want to know. On brain waves (w1894-2059) he hedges the numbers himself ("I can't remember"); the block keeps the hedge.

Line 26: he first calls the passage from the lungs the veshet (esophagus), then takes the listener's "windpipe" (w2497-2568); the block follows windpipe. In the wind-instrument mashal a listener supplies "stretches" and "causes the larynx to vibrate".
The forty days before birth (206 w3756-3793) are not named as a source by him; the block says "it is said". Rashi on Esav asking how to tithe salt and straw is his reference (207 w287-311).

Line 48: the phrase for "הוא מתייחד בלאה התחתונה" cites his whole rendering (w1249-1285), which says both "not the upper Leah" and "but the actual machshava". The printed line has "מוחין דאבא ואמא"; he reads "מוחין דאבא" only.
Line 52's phrase cut: "ומן המחשבה בא אל הלב, בחיצוניות הבל הלב" is split at the first "הלב" because the word repeats; his one sentence (w2630-2645) is split across the two phrases.

Lines 57-58 and 61 are read without a translation of their own; 57-58 are joined to the passage on the order of the flow. Line 61 he renders only as "In Shabbos, it's holiness" (207 w3498-3501), which is a gloss, so the phrase has no English.
